offers_products.reason: It sells insurance policies, which count as a financial service, not manufactured goods or software.

offers_services.reason: Specialty property and casualty insurance (earthquake, casualty, inland marine, crop, surety); insurers count as services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Provides residential earthquake and catastrophe insurance to individuals and homeowners, as well as commercial clients.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Commercial earthquake, E&S casualty, inland marine, surety and crop policies are sold to businesses.

recurring_revenue.reason: Premiums come from annually renewing insurance policies on earthquake, casualty and property coverage.

cyclical_demand.reason: Earthquake, casualty, surety and crop insurance are needed protection, often required by lenders or contracts, so it's rarely cut in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Insurance premiums are modest, recurring payments, not large infrequent purchases like homes or machinery.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for risk coverage backed by balance-sheet capital, not for staff time and skill.

large_customers.reason: Customers are individual homeowners and mostly small and mid-sized businesses, written through agents and programs, not mainly large enterprises.

asset_heavy.reason: Insurer's capital is financial; it needs no plants or fleets, writing policies through underwriting and distribution partners.

notes: Palomar is a specialty P&C insurer. Its larger business is probably residential and commercial earthquake and other property cover.
